physical: A wave passing through an aperture spreads; the narrower the aperture compared with the wavelength, the wider the spread. sin θ ≈ λ ÷ a
reflected_formula: sin θ ≈ λ ÷ a (kept as given; θ, λ and a have no frozen partners)
reflected_sentence: The formula keeps its form, but its reading turns around: what got harder the narrower the opening now gets easier the more receptive the opening, so where a wave was made to spread, the Current meets the gap and collecting widens instead.
rule_reason: Separation made by distance: the cost 'passing through without spreading' is flagged as a separation cost and the aperture width carries distance; one such cost, odd parity, turns the reading.
interpretation: Radiation reflects to collection, so the spread of the wave reads as a widening collection. What a narrowing opening made hard, receptivity makes easy. The quantities themselves have no partners, so only the relationship crosses and the symbols stay bare.
closing: The rule decided on its own: the cost entry flags a separation made by distance, and separations turn by rule, so no judgment call was needed. The loss is that angle, wavelength and aperture width have no partners, so the formula crosses only as symbols and the reflection stays thin. The alternate statement with no named difficulty would keep, but the relation as given turns.

physical: In a dispersive medium the phase velocity depends on wavelength, so a pulse made of many wavelengths spreads as it travels. v_p = v_p(λ)
reflected_formula: rise per Expansion = rise per Expansion(λ) (λ kept as a symbol with no partner)
reflected_sentence: The dependence keeps its shape: the rise per Expansion of a wave depends on its extent, and a pulse of many extents spreads all the same, because what drives the spreading is a dependence, not an opposition.
rule_reason: The single cost ('a pulse keeping its shape') rises with dispersion, and the fixed table says dispersion does not carry resistance — 'a dependence, not an opposition'; zero resistance-caused costs, even parity, so it keeps.
interpretation: A dependence is not an opposition, so the spread of a many-extent pulse crosses unchanged. The rise per Expansion follows the extent and no gap appears. Wavelength has no partner and remains a bare symbol.
closing: The fixed table settled it without me: dispersion is explicitly not an opposition, so the named cost is not caused by resistance and the even-parity rule keeps the shape. No judgment call was needed; the only weakness is that wavelength and dispersion have no partners.

physical: A receiver moving toward a source, or a source moving toward a receiver, measures a higher frequency than the one emitted; moving apart, a lower one. f' = f × (v + v_r) ÷ (v − v_s)
reflected_formula: f' = f × (rise per Expansion + rise per Expansion) ÷ (rise per Expansion − rise per Expansion) (f and f' kept as symbols with no partner)
reflected_sentence: With no cost named, the relation keeps its shape: an approach still raises and a parting still lowers, only now it is rises per Expansion trading against rises per Expansion while the counted rate has no partner and stays a symbol.
rule_reason: No costs at all; an equation among rates and a physical frequency, none of which carry resistance; zero resistance-costs, even parity, keeps.
interpretation: Every rate crosses as rise per Expansion and the formula survives verbatim. But the physical frequency has no partner, so the equation no longer says anything countable. The shape holds; the content thins to near-nothing.
closing: The rule decided alone: no costs, even parity, keeps. Nothing was ambiguous; the reflection is simply thin because physical frequency, wave speed and the two velocities collapse onto one frozen phrase, leaving a formula that adds and subtracts the same words.

physical: At an interface between two media part of the light reflects and part transmits; the reflected fraction grows with the index contrast and the two fractions sum to one. R = ((n1 − n2) ÷ (n1 + n2))²
reflected_formula: R = ((n1 − n2) ÷ (n1 + n2))² (kept as given; R, n1 and n2 have no frozen partners)
reflected_sentence: The formula keeps its form but its reading turns around: what got harder the more the two media differed now gets easier with receptivity, and the share held back at the gap shrinks as the two media meet in the Current rather than oppose.
rule_reason: The cost 'getting through the boundary' rises with index contrast; judged to carry resistance here on Ch 16's medium-as-resistance reading, making one resistance-cost, odd parity, so the reading turns while the formula stays.
interpretation: The word for the surface may not cross, so the gap takes its part. What the contrast held back now passes as receptivity grows, and the two shares still sum to one because the conservation was an identity. Only the difficulty turned.
closing: Judgment call, and it decides everything: refractive index and index contrast are both marked UNDETERMINED. I read the medium as resistance, as Ch 16 does, since the named cost is literally 'getting through' and rises with the contrast; that makes one resistance-cost and the relation turns. Under the ratio-of-speeds reading no resistance-cost exists and the same formula would keep instead — the rule declined to choose.

physical: The envelope of a wave packet travels at the group velocity, the derivative of angular frequency with respect to wavenumber; it is the speed at which energy and signal travel. v_g = dω ÷ dk
reflected_formula: rise per Expansion = dω ÷ dk (ω and k kept as symbols with no partners)
reflected_sentence: As a definition it keeps its shape: the rise per Expansion of the envelope is the change of the counted rate per change of the inverse extent, and the envelope of conscious energy still sets how fast the news of it goes.
rule_reason: It is a definition; definitions keep their shape; no costs named.
interpretation: A definition crosses whole. Rise per Expansion stands where group velocity stood and the derivative form survives. With ω and k unmapped, the right side is two bare symbols joined by ÷.
closing: The rule decided alone: definitions keep. No ambiguity; the result is a formally intact but semantically thin reflection, since only the velocity term finds a partner.

physical: A wave's phase advances by one cycle per wavelength; the phase velocity is wavelength times frequency, or angular frequency over wavenumber. v_p = ω ÷ k
reflected_formula: rise per Expansion = ω ÷ k (ω and k kept as symbols with no partners)
reflected_sentence: As a definition it keeps its shape: one cycle per extent still advances the phase, and the rise per Expansion is the counted rate divided by the inverse extent.
rule_reason: It is a definition; definitions keep their shape; no costs named.
interpretation: The definition crosses whole: a counted rate over an inverse extent is a rise per Expansion. Both right-side symbols lack partners, so the sentence carries the shape and nothing more.
closing: Definitions keep, so no judgment was needed; the reflection is shape without content because ω, k and phase all lack partners.

physical: Crossing into a medium with a different refractive index, a ray bends so that index times the sine of the angle is the same on both sides. n1 × sin θ1 = n2 × sin θ2
reflected_formula: n1 × sin θ1 = n2 × sin θ2 (kept as given; n and θ have no frozen partners)
reflected_sentence: It keeps its shape: what matches on the two sides of a crossing still matches, since the balance of a slowing factor times a bend measure is an invariance and names no difficulty.
rule_reason: An invariance ('the same on both sides') with no cost named; equivalences and conservations keep their shape.
interpretation: The invariance crosses whole even though neither n nor θ has a partner. Bending becomes a matching of two bare symbols. No gap appears because no opposition was named.
closing: The relation as given names no cost, so even parity keeps it and the UNDETERMINED status of refractive index never had to be settled. Slightly less clean than the pure definitions, because 'crossing into a different medium' flirts with opposition, but the statement names none and strictness says to take it as given.

physical: Between two fixed ends only wavelengths that fit a whole number of half-waves into the length persist; the ends force nodes and the allowed modes are set by the separation. λ_n = 2 × L ÷ n
reflected_formula: λ_n = 2 × L ÷ n (kept as given; λ, L and n have no frozen partners)
reflected_sentence: The formula keeps its form but the limit turns around: where a separation let only the fitting vibrations persist, no separation crosses the mirror, so the limited reads as limitless and every vibration is already welcome.
rule_reason: A limit whose selection is set by a separation made by distance (the length between the ends, flagged as a separation); one separation, odd parity, turns the reading, and limited reflects to limitless.
interpretation: Length is a separation and separations do not cross. The fence of nodes is the gap's work, and without the fence the selection dissolves. What was limited is limitless.
closing: The cost entry flags the selection as a separation made by distance, and separations turn by rule, so no judgment was needed. The reflection even has frozen vocabulary for the turn (limited to limitless), which makes it cleaner than most of this batch, though none of the three symbols finds a partner.

physical: In a linear medium the net displacement at any point is the sum of the displacements each wave would produce alone. y = y1 + y2
reflected_formula: y = y1 + y2 (kept as given; y has no frozen partner)
reflected_sentence: It keeps its shape: the net vibration is the sum of what each vibration brings alone, and on the nonphysical side two vibrations do more than add — they culminate, since the book itself has a sum here and the sum crosses whole.
rule_reason: It is an identity in a linear medium; identities keep their shape; no costs named.
interpretation: An identity crosses whole, sum and all, because the book itself writes a sum here. Culminate is the frozen word for what two vibrations do together. Amplitude never finds a partner.
closing: The rule decided alone: an identity with no costs keeps. The trap about sums does not bite because the physical relation itself is a sum. Ch 16's word culminate fits without stretching, which lifts this row above the bare-symbol rows.

physical: Going from a higher to a lower index, beyond the critical angle no light crosses the boundary; all of it is reflected, while an evanescent field reaches past the surface without carrying energy across. sin θ_c = n2 ÷ n1
reflected_formula: sin θ_c = n2 ÷ n1 (kept as given; θ_c and n have no frozen partners)
reflected_sentence: The formula keeps its form but the limit turns around: what read as a slant past which no light may cross now reads as a mark past which nothing is held back — the unreachable is already there, and what the gap returned now collects.
rule_reason: The cost 'crossing the boundary' rises with refractive index; judged to carry resistance here, making one resistance-cost, odd parity, so the reading turns while the formula stays.
interpretation: The banned word for the surface becomes the gap. A cost that rises with the medium's opposition flips to an ease that rises with receptivity. What was all returned now collects.
closing: Judgment call, the same one as the Fresnel row: refractive index is UNDETERMINED, and the turn depends entirely on reading the medium as resistance, which Ch 16's diffraction line supports and the ratio-of-speeds definition denies. I took the resistance reading because the statement's own cost rises with the index; on the other reading this row has zero costs of the relevant kind and would keep.

physical: Two waves in opposite phase cancel at a point; the cancellation is located, and energy is conserved overall. (no formula)
reflected_sentence: The relation turns around: two vibrations set against each other do not cancel at all, they culminate, and the conscious energy that an account of cancellation had to keep safe is simply E, shared by both sides.
rule_reason: The cost 'two vibrations coexisting at one location' is a separation made by distance (the cancellation is located and carried by length); one separation, odd parity, turns the reading.
interpretation: A located cancellation needs a separation, and separations do not cross. The frozen vocabulary already contains the turn: culminate is what two vibrations do instead of cancel. Conservation needs no rescue because E keeps the energy on both sides.
closing: The rule decided alone: the cost entry flags a separation made by distance and odd parity turns it. Unusually, the frozen vocabulary confirms the turned reading word for word, since culminate is defined as what two vibrations do instead of cancel; this is the one row where the reflection says something the table already half-said.
